evidence: Manual application of check-probe-not-in-seed (the private checker executable was not run). (1) The seed is empty: environment/assets/seed_data.json:2 has "snippets": [] and only a prose note. (2) The reference starts with no records: solution/solve.sh:37 removes /app/app.db*, and server.js:147-168 only creates tables (the single INSERT OR IGNORE at :167-168 copies existing snippet rows into the revision table; it inserts no content). (3) The reference's initial UI state is an empty editor, title 'Untitled', filename 'snippet.js', status 'Ready', an empty console and an empty library (solution/app/src/app.tsx:22-26, :33, and the placeholder strings in the library and console markup). (4) Almost every probe value is chosen by the judge at run time: functional/prompt.md:23 'You may choose the exact fixture text for each criterion. Check that the editor holds it before acting', and the criteria ask for 'unique title', 'distinctive message', 'distinctive marker', integers 'you choose'. app_context.md:21 additionally tells the judge not to assume an empty library and that records are identified by the server, not by title. (5) The only literal probe value fixed by a criterion is 'MULTI' (functional/judge.toml:101, cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic); a case-sensitive grep of the whole frozen task finds it only on that line - not in the seed, the reference source, the built bundle public/assets/index.js, or runner.html. (6) Persistence criteria (cw_shared_saved_record, cw_save_reload_restart, stale-save, history, live-update) all require a judge-created unique title and source, so the default 'Untitled'/'snippet.js' values cannot stand in for a saved mutation. Observation, not a defect of this row: the reference footer permanently shows '5s run budget' (app.tsx keyboard-help footer) while several criteria require that 'a visible time-limit reason must appear'; the reference also emits a real reason ('Execution stopped: five-second time limit', runtime.ts:141 and :374), and the criteria word it as something that appears after the run, so the reference is not pre-satisfying its own probe. No configured judge run exists to show how the judge treats static text; that is outside this row.
